links.comparator_used: Single model for all items: Jev decision model alone (94.4%) or the general LLM alone (99.0%)
links.outcome: Item-level NIHSS scoring accuracy against the synthetic answer key (simulated confidence-based routing of uncertain Jev items to the LLM)
links.effect: Re-checking the 14.8% of items with Jev confidence below 0.70 would have caught 86% of Jev's errors; the simulated hybrid reached 98.8% accuracy, versus 94.4% for Jev alone and 99.0% for the LLM alone
links.tradeoff: The hybrid was simulated, not run live. The LLM is slower and costlier than Jev (median 5.78 vs 0.15 s per exam; USD 0.67 vs 0.23 per 1,000 exams). No cost or latency was reported for the hybrid itself.
links.quote: Re-checking the 14.8% of items with confidence below 0.70 would have caught 86% of them, and a simulated hybrid reached 98.8% accuracy.

design_hint: confidence-threshold routing of uncertain items to LLM review
